wa_abernathy_peak_north_ridge.cal: The ridge and the slopes above the tarn can hold snow into early summer; most parties climb it July-October.

days.note: About 10 miles of up-and-down trail up the Wolf Creek valley, through forest burned in 2021, to the meadows at the end of the Wolf Creek Trail. The trail drops a couple of hundred feet right after the trailhead, which has to be regained at the very end of the trip.
days.title: Hike Wolf Creek to Gardner Meadows

schedule.label: Camp at Gardner Meadows
schedule.detail: Established sites near the end of the trail; more flat spots in the trees by the creek.

days.objective: Reach camp at Gardner Meadows

days.note: Cross Wolf Creek from the last campsites and follow a faint path that soon fades into old burn. Keep high above Abernathy Lake and traverse up into the upper basin with the small tarn and the remains of a mining camp. Climb the spur ridge from the tarn to the main north ridge (a few exposed class 3 moves), follow a short boot path past old mining debris on the crest, then scramble class 2-3 boulders and scree to the summit. Descend by the scree slope or the old path back to the tarn, return to camp and either hike out or spend a second night.
days.title: North ridge scramble, then out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Cross Wolf Creek and head for the upper tarn, staying above Abernathy Lake.

schedule.label: Spur ridge to the north ridge
schedule.detail: A few exposed class 3 moves; then a short boot path past old mining debris.

schedule.label: Summit (8,321 ft)
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 boulders and scree along the crest.

schedule.label: Back to camp
schedule.detail: Scree slope or the old path down to the tarn; then retrace the line to Gardner Meadows.

days.objective: Summit via the tarn, the spur ridge and the north ridge

wa_abernathy_peak_north_ridge.totalNote: A remote trip, usually done with a night at Gardner Meadows: about 10 miles of trail each way, then an off-trail climb from the meadows to the summit and back.

wa_cinderella_peak_scramble.cal: The Middle Fork Nooksack bridge/log crossing at the start of the Elbow Lake Trail washes out periodically - check recent trip reports before relying on a dry crossing.

days.note: Walk or bike the 4 closed miles of FR 38 from the washout to the Elbow Lake trailhead first. Fit parties often do this as one long car-to-car day; others camp in the Green Creek basin. While FS Road 38 is closed by its washout, biking the closed road miles saves the legs. From the trailhead, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack, hike the Elbow Lake Trail through old growth to the Hildebrand Creek switchback, and follow the blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' trail into the cirque, across the low-angle glacier to the Cinderella-Little Sister notch and up the west ridge on grippy olivine rock to the summit. Descend by reversing the route, including re-biking the closed road miles at the end.
days.title: Bike/hike approach and ridge scramble to the summit

schedule.label: Leave car, bike the logging road
schedule.detail: FS Road 38 is closed by a washout at milepost 7, about 4 miles short of the trailhead; biking those closed miles saves time and legs.

schedule.label: Stash bikes, start Elbow Lake Trail on foot
schedule.detail: Cross the Middle Fork Nooksack right at the trailhead (no bridge), then climb through old growth above the Green Creek valley about 1.5 mi to the Hildebrand Creek switchback, where the blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' trail branches off.

schedule.label: Reach the Green Creek cirque
schedule.detail: Talus, loose scree and Class 3 rock steps lead to the toe of the glacier; cross it to the notch between Cinderella and Little Sister.

schedule.label: Ridge/gully scramble to Cinderella summit
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 scrambling on solid, high-friction olivine rock; some exposed ridge sections and route-finding around gendarmes.

schedule.label: Reverse the scramble and hike back to bikes
schedule.detail: Downclimb the ridge, retrace the glacier, the Green Creek climbers' trail and the Elbow Lake Trail.

schedule.label: Bike out to the car
schedule.detail: Mostly downhill/flat closed-road miles back to the vehicle.

days.objective: Summit Cinderella Peak via the west ridge olivine scramble, car-to-car

wa_cinderella_peak_scramble.totalNote: A long single push: roughly 11-12 hours car-to-car, ~12 miles and ~5,400 ft of gain, done in a day, as many fit parties do.

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.cal: North Cascades NP requires a backcountry permit for Terror/Crescent Creek Basin camps, and the Barrier is normally only safely crossable July-September once seasonal snow bridges and the approach brush have opened up.

days.note: A grueling cross-country day: old roadbed and steep, brushy boot path from Goodell Creek Trailhead past Terror Creek, then a loose, exposed scramble across the Barrier into the Crescent Creek Basin drainage. Most parties camp on a flat bench or col around 6,000-6,400 ft, close under the Chopping Block/Twin Needles group.
days.title: Approach over the Barrier to high camp

schedule.label: Leave Goodell Creek Trailhead
schedule.detail: Follow the old logging roadbed roughly 4 miles before it fades into boot-path.

schedule.label: Ford Terror Creek, start steep climber's path
schedule.detail: Very steep, root- and brush-choked trail gaining toward treeline.

schedule.label: Cross the Barrier
schedule.detail: Loose, exposed ledges and talus at ~6,000-6,400 ft; the crux of the approach and route-finding.

schedule.label: Arrive high camp
schedule.detail: Camp near the Chopping Block col or on benches above Crescent Creek Basin.

days.objective: Reach camp in/above Crescent Creek Basin

days.note: An alpine-start day from camp: cross Crescent Creek Basin's snow and talus to Eye Col, the notch between the two Twin Needles, then scramble/climb the South Route to East Twin Needle's summit. Most parties use the same col to tack on West Twin Needle's easier class 2-3 west slope before returning to camp.
days.title: East (and West) Twin Needle via Eye Col

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Alpine start to cross snow/talus in basin while firm.

schedule.label: Gain Eye Col
schedule.detail: Loose gully between the two Needles: small chockstones low down are scrambled, the bigger ones higher up are fifth class and usually pitched out, then a short scree walk to the col.

schedule.label: South Route to East Twin Needle summit
schedule.detail: Steep rock on the summit block directly above the col, with a short hand-crack crux near the top; parties rope up.

schedule.label: Descend to Eye Col, tag West Twin Needle
schedule.detail: Optional: easier class 2-3 west slope from the col if time and weather allow.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse gullies/rappels down to Crescent Creek Basin and camp.

days.objective: Summit East Twin Needle, tag West Twin Needle if conditions allow

days.note: Built-in slack for weather or recovery. Strong parties instead use it to climb another objective from the same camp, commonly Himmelhorn or Mount Terror's West Ridge, at similar cost in time and effort to Day 2.
days.title: Spare day / bonus objective
days.objective: Weather buffer or add a second Southern Pickets peak

days.note: A long reversal of Day 1: break camp, re-cross the Barrier, and descend the steep boot path and roadbed back to the car. Most parties treat this as a full day given the terrain and fatigue.
days.title: Descend back to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek Trailhead

wa_east_twin_needle_south_route.totalNote: A 3-4 day trip out of Goodell Creek Trailhead: a long, brutal cross-country approach over the Barrier to a high camp in/above Crescent Creek Basin, a big summit day tagging East (and usually West) Twin Needle via Eye Col, an optional spare/bonus day, and a long descent back out — roughly 16-19 miles round trip and 7,000+ ft of cumulative gain.

days.note: Up North Fork Sauk Trail #649 through old-growth forest and a long set of switchbacks to the Pacific Crest Trail, then north on the PCT over Red Pass into the upper White Chuck valley.
days.title: North Fork Sauk Trail to the PCT and over Red Pass
days.objective: Reach the PCT and cross Red Pass

days.note: Follow the PCT down the upper White Chuck valley to Sitkum Creek, then take the steep, unsigned climbers' path up the ridge south of the creek to the high camp at Boulder Basin.
days.title: Down the PCT to Sitkum Creek and up to Boulder Basin
days.objective: Reach Boulder Basin (5,500-6,000 ft)

days.note: Rope up from Boulder Basin, climb the heavily crevassed Sitkum Glacier to a saddle near Sitkum Spire (~9,500 ft), then follow the pumice/scree ridge (with one short snow traverse) to the summit before reversing back to camp.
days.title: Summit via the Sitkum Glacier

schedule.label: Leave Boulder Basin
schedule.detail: Rope up for glacier travel.

schedule.label: Reach the ~9,500 ft saddle
schedule.detail: East of Sitkum Spire, at the top of the glacier.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Final stretch is scree/pumice with a short snow-field traverse.

schedule.label: Back at Boulder Basin camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the glacier; watch for softening snow bridges late in the day.

days.objective: Summit Glacier Peak (10,541 ft) and return to camp

days.note: Break camp, descend the climbers' path to the PCT, and walk back up the White Chuck valley and over Red Pass to the North Fork Sauk Trail and the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to trailhead

wa_glacier_peak_sitkum_glacier.totalNote: A 4-day trip at minimum. The walk in from the North Fork Sauk trailhead is far longer than the old White Chuck approach and crosses Red Pass in both directions, so many parties allow an extra day.

wa_half_moon_southwest_slopes.cal: Approach talus is described as best done with snow cover in early spring, or after it melts out by July, since bare talus is exposed and leg-breaking.

days.note: A long day from the road, no camp: from the hairpin pullout on the highway near Washington Pass, follow the cairned climbers' path south, staying above Early Winters Creek. About two miles in, cross the last soggy meadow before the path climbs toward Kangaroo Pass and turn up the talus and scree gully that angles back to the deep notch just north of Half Moon. Climb about seven pitches of the North Ridge to the summit, then rappel the route back to the notch and reverse the approach.
days.title: Car-to-car climb of the North Ridge

schedule.label: Leave the hairpin pullout (Hwy 20, ~MP 163)
schedule.detail: Climbers' path staying west of and above Early Winters Creek.

schedule.label: Leave the path about two miles in
schedule.detail: After the last soggy meadow below Kangaroo Pass, turn up the scree gully that angles back toward the notch north of Half Moon.

schedule.label: Notch north of Half Moon
schedule.detail: Base of the North Ridge.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: About seven pitches on or just west of the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Back at the notch
schedule.detail: Rappel the line of ascent, then descend the gully and reverse the path.

days.objective: Climb the North Ridge of Half Moon and return to the hairpin pullout

wa_half_moon_southwest_slopes.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car with no camp: an off-trail approach, about seven pitches of climbing and a rappel descent.

wa_jack_mountain_south_face.cal: South Face is typically climbed August-September once snow clears the loose rock; overnight camps fall inside the North Cascades NP Complex/Ross Lake NRA backcountry, which requires a wilderness camping permit.

days.note: From the Canyon Creek Trailhead, hike FST 738 through McMillan Park to Crater Lake, then climb to the Crater Mountain saddle, cross/skirt the Jerry Glacier basin, and descend scree and heather to a camp near Crater Creek or the Jerry Lakes basin. This is the long day of the trip, mostly off-trail after the saddle.
days.title: Approach to high camp

schedule.label: Top out at Crater Mountain saddle
schedule.detail: Roughly 4 hrs from the car

schedule.label: Reach camp near Crater Creek Meadows/Jerry Lakes

days.objective: Reach a high camp near Crater Creek Meadows / Jerry Lakes basin (~6,000-6,200 ft)

days.note: Climb from camp up to the ~7,200 ft step in the Southeast Ridge, then pick through loose class 3-4 terrain on the South Face (past the fish-shaped snowfield and hidden chimney) back onto the ridge crest to the summit. Reverse the route to camp; many parties then shuttle gear partway toward the Jerry Lakes saddle in the evening to shorten the exit day.
days.title: Summit day: South Face / SE Ridge

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack

schedule.label: Summit (9,069 ft)
schedule.detail: ~4-4.5 hrs from camp

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the South Face/SE Ridge

schedule.label: Optional camp shuffle
schedule.detail: Some parties relocate toward the Jerry Lakes/6,550 ft saddle to shorten Day 3

days.objective: Climb Jack Mountain (9,069 ft) via the South Face and Southeast Ridge, then reposition camp

days.note: Retrace the approach back over the Jerry Lakes/Crater Mountain saddle area (some parties detour past the East Crater Mountain lookout site) and descend to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out

schedule.label: Pass Crater Mountain saddle / lookout area

days.objective: Return to the Canyon Creek Trailhead

wa_jack_mountain_south_face.totalNote: A 3-day, ~22-24 mile round trip with roughly 11,000-11,500 ft of cumulative gain: one long day to a ~6,000-6,200 ft high camp, one long summit day up the loose South Face/SE Ridge (~9-9.5 hrs camp-to-camp), and one day to hike out.

days.note: The Round the Mountain Trail east from the South Climb trail, then the long, mostly off-trail traverse north round the eastern flank, across the Klickitat Glacier and Big Muddy Creek, to camp in Avalanche Valley below the Rusk and Wilson glaciers.
days.title: Cold Springs to Avalanche Valley
days.objective: Establish camp in Avalanche Valley (~6,600 ft)

days.note: An early alpine start from Avalanche Valley, up the Wilson Glacier to the headwall below Roosevelt Cliff (starts around 10,800 ft) — a steep, avalanche/icefall-fed line considered one of Adams' most serious routes. Top out and descend the South Climb to Cold Springs.
days.title: Climb the headwall, descend to the trailhead

schedule.label: Leave Avalanche Valley
schedule.detail: Early start for firm snow and to minimize icefall exposure below Roosevelt Cliffs.

schedule.label: Descend to the car
schedule.detail: South Climb to Cold Springs.

days.objective: Summit via the Wilson Glacier Headwall and descend fully to the car

wa_mount_adams_wilson_glacier_headwall.totalNote: A 2-day trip: a long approach round the east side to Avalanche Valley, then a serious, early alpine-start headwall climb (~13 hr) and a descent of the South Climb to the car.

wa_mount_challenger_challenger_glacier.cal: Best climbed June-Sept once the Chilliwack River ford, the Impasse and the Challenger Glacier are in reasonable shape; the Ross Lake Resort water taxi (used for the Beaver Pass variant) requires advance reservations.

days.note: From the Hannegan Pass trailhead climb about 2,000 ft in 4 miles to Hannegan Pass, drop past Boundary Camp into the Chilliwack valley, and leave the trail where the faint, unsigned climbers' path for Easy Ridge fords the Chilliwack (log crossings here are unreliable). Climb steeply onto Easy Ridge and camp near the tarns on its crest. A long day with a loaded pack: about 8 hours on foot is typical.
days.title: Hannegan Pass and the Chilliwack to Easy Ridge
days.objective: Camp on the crest of Easy Ridge

days.note: Follow the faint path along the crest over Easy Peak, which has more tent sites and a tarn, to the notch called the Impasse. Where the direct crossing is unsafe, drop off the crest around it and re-climb an exposed class 4 step beyond, then cross the snowfields to Perfect Pass. In fog, keep away from Whatcom Peak's summit wall, which steepens where the pass levels into a saddle.
days.title: Easy Ridge over the Impasse to Perfect Pass
days.objective: Camp at Perfect Pass (about 6,300 ft)

days.note: Get down from Perfect Pass onto the Challenger Glacier (depending on melt-out, about 200 ft of wet class 4 downclimbing and sometimes a short rappel across a moat), rope up, cross the bergschrund and climb steepening snow to the summit rocks, watching for the moat below them. A class 3 scramble leads to the 50 ft, 5.5-5.7 summit pitch; rappel it once and reverse the glacier to Perfect Pass. Some parties pack up the same afternoon and recross the Impasse to shorten the walk out.
days.title: Summit day via the Challenger Glacier
days.objective: Climb Mount Challenger via the Challenger Glacier and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the approach: back along Easy Ridge, down to the Chilliwack ford, and up the long climb to Hannegan Pass before the easy descent to the car.
days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike back out to the Hannegan Pass trailhead

wa_mount_challenger_challenger_glacier.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip via Easy Ridge (add a spare day for weather), with camps on Easy Ridge and at Perfect Pass and one glacier summit day from Perfect Pass.

wa_mount_claywood_standard.cal: Backcountry permits are required for all overnight stays in Olympic National Park (reserve via the Wilderness Information Center/recreation.gov); snow can linger on Grand Pass and the high cross-country sections into July, so most parties go July–September.

days.note: From Obstruction Point Trailhead, follow the Grand Pass Trail along Lillian Ridge and over Grand Pass, drop into Cameron Basin and climb steeply over Cameron Pass, then descend the primitive trail into Lost Basin at the head of the Lost River. Camp is an unmaintained site in Lost Basin (~5,350 ft); the last climb to Cameron Pass is loose and holds snow into midsummer.
days.title: Approach to Lost Basin high camp
days.objective: Reach a rough high camp in Lost Basin below Lost Pass

days.note: Leave the tent at camp and climb steeply to Lost Pass (5,570 ft) between Lost Peak and Claywood, then follow class 2-3 talus and heather slopes west-southwest to the summit before retracing the route back to Lost Basin.
days.title: Summit day: Mount Claywood

schedule.label: Leave Lost Basin camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack; climb toward Lost Pass.

schedule.label: Reach Lost Pass (5,570 ft)
schedule.detail: Col between Lost Peak and Mt Claywood.

schedule.label: Reach the summit scramble
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 talus and heather scrambling begins.

schedule.label: Summit Mount Claywood (6,836 ft)
schedule.detail: Views to Mt Olympus, Mt Cameron, and the Bailey Range.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Retrace the ridge and re-cross Lost Pass.

schedule.label: Back at Lost Basin camp
schedule.detail: Rest, water up, prep for tomorrow's exit.

days.objective: Climb Mount Claywood (6,836 ft) via Lost Pass and return to camp

days.note: Break camp and climb back over Cameron Pass, drop into Cameron Basin, then climb back over Grand Pass before the long descending trail to Obstruction Point. This exit is strenuous in either direction — expect a long, tiring day after two days of off-trail travel.
days.title: Exit via Cameron Pass and Grand Pass
days.objective: Hike out to Obstruction Point Trailhead

wa_mount_claywood_standard.totalNote: A remote 3-day, 2-night backpack (about 28 mi round trip, over Grand Pass and Cameron Pass each way) built around one high camp in Lost Basin below Lost Pass — not a car-to-car day trip given how deep and rugged the approach and exit are.

wa_mount_fairchild_standard.cal: Best from mid-July to early September. Earlier, steep snow can linger on the Catwalk and the Carrie side; later, the glacier runs to bare ice and its snow bridges thin.

days.note: Walk the Sol Duc River Trail past Sol Duc Falls and climb to the High Divide by way of Deer Lake or Heart Lake, then follow the divide east to the Cat Basin junction, where the maintained trail ends. Fill every bottle before leaving the divide trail: the way on toward Cat Peak carries no water. Camp in Cat Basin, the last sheltered ground before the route goes cross-country.
days.title: Sol Duc trailhead to Cat Basin
days.objective: Camp in Cat Basin below Cat Peak

days.note: Leave Cat Basin on the boot path below Cat Peak and cross the Catwalk, the narrow, exposed ridge between Cat Peak and Mount Carrie. With a full pack it is the crux of the approach, and no place to be in wet weather. Camp at Boston Charlie's on the far side, where the only water is a small sinkhole pond that must be filtered.
days.title: Across the Catwalk to Boston Charlie's
days.objective: Camp at Boston Charlie's, at the foot of Mount Carrie

days.note: Climb roughly 2,000 ft from camp to the summit of Mount Carrie. From Carrie's top, rope up and put on crampons, head northeast down onto the glacier, circle round to the north side of Fairchild and climb its Southwest Ridge to the summit. Reverse the whole line back over Carrie to camp, allowing for snow bridges that soften through the afternoon.
days.title: Summit day: over Mount Carrie to Fairchild
days.objective: Summit Mount Fairchild (6,899 ft) and return to Boston Charlie's

days.note: Recross the Catwalk to Cat Basin, regain the High Divide trail and follow it back down past Sol Duc Falls to the trailhead.
days.title: Hike out to Sol Duc
days.objective: Return to the Sol Duc trailhead

wa_mount_fairchild_standard.totalNote: A 4-day, 3-night out-and-back from the Sol Duc trailhead: a trail day to Cat Basin, a short day across the Catwalk to Boston Charlie's, a long summit day over Mount Carrie to Fairchild and back, and a long day out.

wa_mount_mathias_scramble.cal: Needs an Olympic National Park wilderness permit for the nights at Glacier Meadows. The route is in condition roughly July to September, and it goes faster and more safely while the snow finger still holds snow rather than bare ice or scree.

days.note: The long, mostly gentle Hoh River Trail through the rainforest, climbing steadily only in the last few miles out of the valley. A washed-out section near the top is crossed on a fixed ladder. Packs carry full glacier kit.
days.title: Hoh trailhead to Glacier Meadows
days.objective: Reach the Glacier Meadows base camp

days.note: Take the way trail to the Blue Glacier moraine, rope up and cross the glacier to Snow Dome, then continue up the upper Blue Glacier to Glacier Pass, the saddle between Mathias and the East Peak of Mount Olympus. Climb the steep snow finger between Mathias and the pass, or the gullies to the Mercury-Mathias col, to Class 4 rock on the summit ridge. Reverse the climb and recross the glacier to Glacier Meadows. Mount Mercury is often added from the col.
days.title: Blue Glacier, Glacier Pass and the Mathias summit
days.objective: Climb Mount Mathias by the snow finger or the Mercury-Mathias col and return to camp

days.note: A long, mostly downhill trail day back to the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Walk back down the Hoh River Trail to the trailhead

wa_mount_mathias_scramble.totalNote: An out-and-back from the Hoh: a long trail day in to Glacier Meadows, a roped glacier day to Glacier Pass and the summit ridge, and the walk out. Many parties add a spare day for weather or climb Mathias alongside Mount Olympus.

wa_mount_seattle_south.cal: Olympic National Park wilderness permits (quota-based in summer) are required for all backcountry camps along this route; check current park conditions for the North Fork Quinault fords, especially the Sixteen Mile crossing, before committing to the approach.

days.note: From the North Fork Quinault trailhead at road's end, the trail follows the valley floor through old-growth forest past Wolf Bar and Halfway House. Wild Rose Creek and Elip Creek are fords that can run fast in heavy rain or peak snowmelt. Full packs, modest grade — this is mileage-banking, not climbing.
days.title: Up the North Fork Quinault River Trail
days.objective: Reach a river camp such as Elip Creek or Sixteen Mile

days.note: Ford the North Fork at Sixteen Mile (normally knee- to thigh-deep and swift, and hazardous or impassable in heavy rain or snowmelt), then make the steep, loose climb to Low Divide (3,602 ft), the pass between the Quinault and Elwha drainages. Continue into Seattle Creek Basin and up to a meadow camp near 4,550 ft at Seattle Meadows, below the peak's west slopes.
days.title: Over the Sixteen Mile ford to Low Divide and high camp
days.objective: Reach a high camp at Seattle Meadows

days.note: Leave the tent at camp and go light. Climb scree on the peak's western side, cross over the ridge and ascend talus on the eastern side to the east ridge, then Class 2-3 scrambling to the 6,246 ft summit; reverse the same line back to camp.
days.title: Summit day

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Light daypack; rope/overnight gear left at camp.

schedule.label: Gain the south/east ridge
schedule.detail: Talus and scree slopes above Seattle Meadows basin.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Class 2-3 scramble; views across the Bailey Range and Elwha headwaters.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the south-side scree/talus line.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: Rest of the day free to recover before the long walk out begins.

days.objective: Climb Mount Seattle via the south-side talus/scree slopes

days.note: Drop back to Low Divide, descend the steep trail to the Sixteen Mile ford and continue down the North Fork valley as far as is reasonable with a full pack after a summit day.
days.title: Back down to the North Fork
days.objective: Return to a river camp below Low Divide

days.note: Finish down the North Fork Quinault valley to the cars, re-crossing the Elip Creek and Wild Rose Creek fords. A long but easy-grade final day.
days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the North Fork Quinault trailhead

wa_mount_seattle_south.totalNote: A multi-day wilderness backpack (about 5 days / 4 nights) up the North Fork Quinault River, 16 trail miles to Low Divide, then on to a high camp at Seattle Meadows, with a half-day scramble to the 6,246 ft summit and the same trail back out.

wa_olympus_traverse.cal: Glacier Pass has reported icefall hazard and deep snow moats near Middle Peak in recent seasons; conditions vary enough year to year that some parties substitute easier Panic Peak for East Peak.

days.note: Flat old-growth valley approach along the Hoh River.
days.title: Hoh River Trail to Olympus Guard Station
days.objective: Reach Lewis Meadow / Olympus Guard Station camp

days.note: Climb through Elk Lake and the washed-out ladder section to camp; this is base for the multi-peak traverse.
days.title: Guard Station to Glacier Meadows high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp at Glacier Meadows

days.note: A long linkup day: climb the West Peak via the standard Blue Glacier/Snow Dome/Crystal Pass line, descend and re-ascend to Middle Peak, continue to East Peak, then descend to Glacier Meadows via Glacier Pass. Deep moats and icefall hazard near Glacier Pass are commonly reported.
days.title: Traverse West, Middle and East Peaks

schedule.label: Leave Glacier Meadows
schedule.detail: Early start — this is the longest day of the trip by far.

schedule.label: West Peak summit
schedule.detail: Via the standard Blue Glacier/Snow Dome/Crystal Pass line.

schedule.label: Middle Peak summit (7,929 ft)
schedule.detail: Cross via the connecting ridge/glacier; deep snow moats reported on the east side.

schedule.label: East Peak summit (7,762 ft)
schedule.detail: Some parties bail to easier Panic Peak instead if conditions/time are marginal.

schedule.label: Descend via Glacier Pass
schedule.detail: Watch for icefall; this descent has been flagged as hazardous in trip reports.

schedule.label: Back at Glacier Meadows
schedule.detail: A very long day — headlamps likely needed for the final stretch.

days.objective: Link all three Olympus summits and descend to Glacier Pass

days.note: Because the three-peak linkup is long and conditions-dependent (moats, icefall near Glacier Pass), most parties plan a spare day here — used for rest, bad weather, or to finish the traverse if Day 3 ran long.
days.title: Weather/rest buffer day
days.objective: Contingency day at Glacier Meadows

days.note: Full hike back down the Hoh River Trail to the car.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Hoh River trailhead

wa_olympus_traverse.totalNote: A 5-day trip: 2 days up to Glacier Meadows, one very long day linking West, Middle and East peaks via Glacier Pass, a built-in buffer day, and a day to hike out — matching the advice to plan an extra day versus the standard single-summit climb.

days.note: Climb the Cascade Pass trail, then follow the traverse's climbers' path up and over Cache Col and down to camp at Kool-Aid Lake.
days.title: Cascade Pass trailhead to Kool-Aid Lake
days.objective: Reach Kool-Aid Lake, the usual first camp on the traverse

days.note: Cross the exposed Red Ledge below Arts Knoll, rope up for the Middle Cascade Glacier, pass through the Spider–Formidable col and descend to camp at Yang Yang Lakes.
days.title: Kool-Aid Lake to Yang Yang Lakes
days.objective: Reach Yang Yang Lakes, the usual second camp

days.note: Climb back to the Le Conte ridge and up the Le Conte Glacier toward the col at its head beside Sentinel Peak. Leave the traverse here, pass north of Sentinel and head east onto the ridge crest.
days.title: Yang Yang Lakes to the Le Conte–Sentinel col
days.objective: Leave the traverse for the west end of Rimrock Ridge

wa_rimrock_ridge_scramble.totalNote: Three days on the Ptarmigan Traverse reach the col between Le Conte and Sentinel, where the line onto Rimrock Ridge begins. No published account gives a schedule for the ridge itself or for leaving it, so no total length is stated here.
